fact: Mali's specialised cybercrime tribunal sentenced journalist Abdrahamane Keita, publication director of Le Temoin, to two years in prison and 1 million CFA francs damages for a remark about Kidal on a TV programme on 4 June 2026, on charges of regionalist remarks, undermining the State's credit and national unity, and spreading false information through an information system; he had been detained since June and the defence intends to appeal.

Journalist Abdrahamane Keita of Le Temoin was detained on 9 June 2026 over comments on the security situation in northern Mali made on a live media programme, and charged with undermining national unity and the credibility of the state and disseminating false information, says IPI.

Journalist Chahana Takiou, editor of 22 Septembre, was sentenced on 3 August 2026 to 12 months in prison, six suspended, and fined, for undermining the credibility of the state; he had been arrested in June 2026 by the National Cybercrime Unit after criticising its use against journalists at the Pan-African Media Forum in Bamako, says IPI.

Radio and television commentator Mohamed Youssouf Bathily (Ras Bath) was arrested in March 2023 after public comments about the death in custody of a former prime minister and has been in detention since, says IPI.

The trial of Mohamed Youssouf Bathily (Ras Bath) began on 10 August 2026 on charges of criminal association and undermining the credibility of the state through information and communication technologies, says IPI.

The national cybercrime unit sentenced journalist Chahana Takiou, founder-publisher of 22 septembre, to 12 months in prison with 6 suspended for undermining the State's credit through the judicial institution, after he said at the Pan-African Media Forum in June 2026 that journalists should be tried under the press-offence law rather than the cybercrime law.
The Malian Association of Private Print Media Publishers denounced the 5 February 2026 arrest of editor Youssouf Sissoko.

Editor Youssouf Sissoko of L'Alternance was arrested on 5 February 2026, charged and held in Bamako's central prison over an article questioning Niger leader Tiani's statements, per Human Rights Watch.

RSF says the HAC suspended the private radio phone-in programme Allo Klédu for two months from 19 June 2026 over listeners' contributions, and that journalists Takiou and Keïta were arrested in June 2026 and charged under the cybercrime law.
RSF says the Maison de la Presse sharply criticised the detention of the two journalists in June 2026, saying the judiciary had fallen short of creating a space of peace and understanding.
The Southern Africa Litigation Centre says a journalist in Mali was imprisoned "last month" for criticising the authorities.
CPJ reports journalists Chahana Takiou (8 June 2026) and Abdrahamane Keita (9 June) were arrested for criticising authorities, and Youssouf Sissoko got two years in March 2026 over a commentary.

Human Rights Watch reports journalist Chahana Takiou was convicted and sentenced to one year in prison on 3 August 2026 for criticising the prosecution of a fellow journalist; Abdramane Keita was also arrested on 9 June 2026 after comments on television.

Human Rights Watch reports Chahana Takiou, editor of the biweekly 22 Septembre, publicly criticised the authorities for prosecuting journalist Youssouf Sissoko under the cybercrime law rather than the press laws.

The Media Foundation for West Africa reports that the National Cybercrime Court convicted former Prime Minister Moussa Mara on 27 October 2025 over social media posts of solidarity with political prisoners, with a two-year sentence, one year firm.

RFI reports that Mali's courts sentenced L'Alternance director Youssouf Sissoko in March 2026 to two years in prison and a one million FCFA fine for publishing an article doubting statements by Niger's President Tiani, with an appeal hearing due on 5 October 2026.

MFWA says the Bamako Court of Appeal on 17 August 2026 sentenced radio commentator Ras Bath and activist Rose Vie Chère to ten years, three suspended, over broadcast comments on inflation and power outages.

MFWA says editor Abdrahamane Keita was detained by the National Cybercrime Unit on 9 June 2026 after a television appearance and remanded in custody on charges including 'dissemination of false information'.
MFWA says Mali's government formally banned distribution, sale and online circulation of Jeune Afrique in January 2026.

Jeune Afrique says the Malian authorities banned distribution of the magazine on 17 January 2026, accusing it of apology for terrorism, defamation and incitement to hatred over its coverage, including of the fuel crisis.
Jeune Afrique says Malian readers report its website has been blocked since late January 2026, and that the authorities have not officially announced the block.

CIVICUS Monitor reports that civil society leader Aliou Badra Sacko's Front Touche pas a mon argent was meeting to counter the newly introduced mobile money and telecommunications taxes when he was abducted.
